title: Can you find the right buckets for these 20 quick case prompts?
description: Twenty short case prompts with the buckets a strong candidate might use. Cover the answer, try your own, then compare.
hook: Here are twenty short case prompts with the buckets a strong candidate might use. Read the prompt, cover the answer, and try your own first.
body:
1. A national bank's mortgage applications are down 20%. Why?

Show the buckets
  • Market (rates, house prices)
  • Our pricing vs rivals
  • Channel (brokers, online)
  • Approval process

2. Should a hotel group launch a budget brand?

Show the buckets
  • Market attractiveness
  • Cannibalisation of current hotels
  • Economics per hotel
  • Capabilities & brand risk

3. A hospital's emergency waiting times have doubled.

Show the buckets
  • Demand (volume, case mix)
  • Capacity (staff, beds)
  • Process (triage, handovers)
  • Outflow (beds upstairs)

4. How should a newspaper grow digital subscriptions?

Show the buckets
  • Reach (traffic, new audiences)
  • Convert free → paid (paywall, price)
  • Retain (engagement, bundles)
  • Revenue per subscriber (tiers, add-ons)

5. Should a car maker build its own battery plant?

Show the buckets
  • Demand & security of supply
  • Make vs buy economics
  • Technology risk
  • Partners/JV

6. A fashion retailer's online returns cost too much.

Show the buckets
  • Return rate by product/size
  • Cost per return
  • Root causes (fit, photos)
  • Policy levers

7. Should a city introduce a congestion charge?

Show the buckets
  • Objectives (traffic, pollution, revenue)
  • Impact on residents & businesses
  • Alternatives
  • Implementation

8. How would you value a football club?

Show the buckets
  • Revenue streams (media, match-day, commercial)
  • Costs (wages)
  • Multiples of comparable deals
  • Strategic premium

9. A pharma company's new drug is selling below forecast.

Show the buckets
  • Doctors (awareness, prescribing)
  • Patients (access, price)
  • Payers (reimbursement)
  • Competition

10. Should an airline start a loyalty credit card?

Show the buckets
  • Customer value
  • Economics (bank payments per point)
  • Partner choice
  • Brand risk

11. A ski resort's profits fell after two warm winters.

Show the buckets
  • Revenue (visitors × spend, by season)
  • Costs (fixed vs flexible)
  • Snow risk (snowmaking, altitude)
  • Other income (summer, events)

12. How can a university increase international students?

Show the buckets
  • Markets & demand
  • Offer (courses, price, rankings)
  • Visas & policy
  • Recruitment channels

13. A food-delivery start-up is burning cash. What do you cut?

Show the buckets
  • Unit economics per order
  • Fixed costs
  • Marketing efficiency (CAC)
  • City-by-city profitability

14. Should a supermarket open dark stores for 15-min delivery?

Show the buckets
  • Demand density
  • Economics per order
  • Cannibalisation
  • Operations & competition

15. A government wants more women in the workforce.

Show the buckets
  • Barriers (childcare, flexibility, norms)
  • Employers
  • Policy levers
  • Measurement

16. How should an electricity company prepare for rooftop solar?

Show the buckets
  • Lost demand
  • Grid costs
  • New services (batteries, EV)
  • Pricing & regulation

17. A cinema chain's attendance has not recovered.

Show the buckets
  • Content supply
  • Customer experience & price
  • Streaming substitution
  • Alternative uses of space

18. Should a coffee brand sell in supermarkets?

Show the buckets
  • Brand risk
  • Incremental revenue vs cannibalisation of cafés
  • Retailer economics
  • Operations

19. A logistics company's on-time delivery fell to 85%.

Show the buckets
  • Where in the chain (pickup, hub, last mile)
  • Capacity vs volume
  • Process and systems
  • External factors (weather, partners)

20. How would you increase organ donor registrations?

Show the buckets
  • Awareness
  • Ease of sign-up (opt-out vs opt-in)
  • Trust
  • Channels (licences, GPs)
outro: Come back to these in a week and try them again. You will be surprised how much quicker the structures come.
